_target_note: Everything below is G17P-direct. Nothing ran on the M4. Where a G16G fact is referenced it is cited as the prior, not as evidence.

imad.b9[bit3] :: addend-source-class sel.encoding_geometry: ledger-verified (6440/6440 requested==decoded from re-read actual bytes; 964 + 548 distinct actual encodings == distinct requested)
imad.b9[bit3] :: addend-source-class sel.semantics: semantically-mapped over the tested domain: sel==0 -> A = IDX (immediate); sel==1 -> A = FILE[IDX]. sel=bit3 scores 2054/2054 and 1158/1158; the rival sel=bit1 scores 1040/2054 and 648/1158
imad.b9[bit3] :: addend-source-class sel.reproducibility: independently-confirmed (two orders per carrier, 100.0000% payload agreement, two carriers, two seed sets)
imad.b9[bit3] :: addend-source-class sel.range: b9 = 0x20..0x2f dense (all 16 low-nibble values with bit5=1) x K = 0..31 dense x 2 seed sets; plus b9 = 0x06/0x0e as the bit5-clear control

imad.b9[bit0] :: fetch width, and the 32.semantics: semantically-mapped: (b9&1)==1 reads a 32-bit WORD at index IDX & ~1, i.e. the index's LOW BIT IS IGNORED. 64/64 word vs 54/64 pair (C-DAG) and 64/64 vs 38/64 (C-CONST); all 36 discriminating odd-K cases say word, in every run
imad.b9[bit0] :: fetch width, and the 32.reproducibility: independently-confirmed (two carriers with completely different constant files, two orders each)
imad.b9[bit0] :: fetch width, and the 32.range: b9 = 0x2f x K = 0..31 dense x 2 seed sets x 2 carriers

imad.mulsel[bits 0..2] :: the addend fie.semantics: bounded-map. IMMEDIATE mode: A = ((b8&7)<<5) | K over all 256 values, 512/512 on each carrier in each run -- G17P-direct, all 32 K, which EXP-0218 had only on G16G. FETCH mode: the same bits are the INDEX's high bits, refuting the 5-bit-index-plus-suppression reading (190/224 held out against a prediction derived from our own MSL source). BOUNDED: bits 0 and 1 are directly demonstrated (indices 0..75); BIT 2 IS STILL UNDECIDABLE because no carrier's file reaches half-index 128
imad.mulsel[bits 0..2] :: the addend fie.range: b8 = 0xd0..0xd7 x K = 0..31 dense x b9 in {0x26, 0x2e} x 2 seed sets x 2 carriers = 2048 records
imad.mulsel[bits 0..2] :: the addend fie.settles: EXP-0218 sections 6.2 and 6.4, the first PARTIALLY
imad.mulsel[bits 0..2] :: the addend fie.open: does any carrier place a non-zero value at half-index >= 128?

imad.b9[bits 1,2,4,6,7].liveness: accepted-inert FOR THE ADDEND in the tested envelope (bit 1 and bit 2: 0 of 64 flip pairs move the addend across the whole b9 x K cross product, both seed sets, both runs); global role unknown
imad.b9[bits 1,2,4,6,7].detection_power: the SAME arm shows bit 3 moving the addend in 64 of 64 flip pairs and the bit5-clear control producing silent_zero, so the observable demonstrably can move

imad :: external constant file (a FINITE.semantics: bounded-map. For kernels/carrier_const.metal the readable file is 76 halves (38 words), populated at half-indices 0..2 and 12..75; every one of the 256 dispatchable indices is single-valued; indices 76..255 read 0 with NO wrap, NO alias, NO fault and NO hang. For EXP-0160's carrier_dag it is populated only at 0..2 and 12..15. THE FILE'S CONTENTS ARE CARRIER STATE, NOT A HARDWARE FACT; what is a hardware fact is the indexing rule and the excess-capacity behaviour

tex_sample.mode[bit6].encoding_geometry: ledger-verified (38974/38974 requested==decoded across every part-B capture); the 14-byte span is a HARDWARE-HONOURED BOUNDARY at all nine arm sites (stop-ruler, one-sided claim)
tex_sample.mode[bit6].liveness: LIVE on 4 of 9 arms (tex_sample@msread/0, msread/1, mslodq/0, mslodq/1 -- 112, 112, 116 and 20 of 128 flip pairs) and ACCEPTED-INERT on 5 (msfilt/0, mscmp/0, msread/2, mslodq/2, msread1/0 -- 0 of 128 each) in the tested envelope. The partition is identical in all four captures
tex_sample.mode[bit6].semantics: hypothesis, NOT a map. It is NOT the sample-operation-class selector db.json's enum implies. Where live it makes the destination write conditional on a device-side state that CYCLES WITH PERIOD 4 OR 8 IN THE DISPATCH INDEX, at pixel/quad granularity: the two outcomes at a given phase are 'the channel is written' and 'the channel is not written, or only its high 16-bit half is'. 240 of 240 alternating sequences have smallest period 4 or 8; 0 aperiodic; confirmed OUT OF SAMPLE at N=24 and with a single GPU context. WHAT THE PERIODIC STATE IS remains UNKNOWN
tex_sample.mode[bit6].reproducibility: independently-confirmed for the PARTITION and the PERIOD STRUCTURE (4 captures, 3 orders, 2 repeat counts, 1- and 5-context). NOT reproducible as payload equality, and cannot be: the observable is a function of the dispatch index, so EXP-0213's Gate E criterion is unmeetable for this field on any machine
tex_sample.mode[bit6].range: full 256-value sweep on 9 arms in 2 orders; plus 65 matched values x 16 or 24 repeats x 9 arms in 3 captures
tex_sample.mode[bit6].actionable: AN EMITTER MUST NOT SET tex_sample.mode BIT 6. On a carrier where it is live the same program returns a different answer on successive draws.
tex_sample.mode[bit6].settles: EXP-0213 section 2.5 -- as a CHARACTERISATION. It explains the Gate E failure; it does not clear Gate E, and it does not map the field

tex_sample.mode[bit7].liveness: accepted-inert in the tested envelope: 0 of 128 flip pairs on EVERY one of nine arms across five carriers, two orders; global role unknown
tex_sample.mode[bit7].detection_power: every one of the nine arms shows bits 2 and 3 moving the same observable in the same capture

db_defects.DEF-0219-1: The committed `imad.mulsel` note records 'in the byte+9 bit3 == 1 branch on G17P, a non-zero low nibble instead yields addend 0 in 68/68 cases -- consistent BOTH with an 8-bit source index whose file is empty above half-index 31 AND with a 5-bit index plus suppression'. The 5-bit reading is now REFUTED on hardware: with kernels/carrier_const.metal, whose file reaches half-index 75, b8's low bits index the file (190/224 held out against an MSL-source prediction), while EXP-0160's carrier reproduces the 0-of-512 artefact in the same captures. The 68/68 observation stands; its generalisation does not. NOT PROPOSED as an edit -- the orchestrator owns db.json.
db_defects.DEF-0219-2: The committed `imad.b9` note says the 32-bit value 'was predicted out-of-sample from the 16-bit table as FILE[K] | FILE[K+1]<<16 and confirmed 6/6'. That is right at EVEN K only. At odd K the hardware reads the WORD at index K & ~1: 36 discriminating cases across two carriers and four captures, 100% word, 0% pair. NOT PROPOSED as an edit.
db_defects.DEF-0219-3: The committed `tex_sample.mode` enum and note call the field a bitfield whose live mask is 'AT MOST 0x2C'. Bit 6 is LIVE on four of nine arms measured here (112/128, 112/128, 116/128 and 20/128 flip pairs), so the live mask on those carriers is at least 0x6C. Bit 7 is inert on all nine. NOT PROPOSED as an edit; and bit 6's liveness must not be documented without the fact that its effect is dispatch-index-periodic and must not be emitted.
